dorsal scapular nerve: Arises from C5 and supplies the rhomboids and levator scapulae.
eyeball: The eyeball; formed by the sclera and cornea outside, the uvea in the middle and the retina inside.
facial nerve (vii): Supplies the muscles of facial expression, taste from the anterior two thirds of the tongue, the lacrimal and salivary glands and stapedius. It leaves through the stylomastoid foramen; a peripheral palsy affects the whole half of the face (Bell's palsy).
falx cerebri: Sickle-shaped fold of dura descending between the hemispheres; it carries the superior and inferior sagittal sinuses.
femoral branch of genitofemoral nerve: Carries sensation from the skin over the femoral triangle (the afferent limb of the cremasteric reflex).
femoral nerve: Largest branch of the lumbar plexus, from L2–L4; supplies quadriceps, sartorius and iliacus and carries the patellar reflex. In the femoral triangle it lies lateral to the artery.
flocculus: Small lobule beside the middle cerebellar peduncle; with the nodule it forms the vestibulocerebellum and regulates eye movements.
folium of vermis: Thin lobule in the posterior superior vermis.
fornix: Arched fibre bundle from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies; the main output pathway of the Papez circuit.
fourth ventricle: Tent-shaped cavity between the pons and medulla and the cerebellum; it opens into the subarachnoid space through the foramina of Magendie and Luschka.
ganglia of sympathetic trunk: Paravertebral ganglia containing the cell bodies of sympathetic postganglionic neurons; the stellate ganglion lies at C7–T1.
genital branch of genitofemoral nerve: Passes through the inguinal canal; supplies cremaster and the skin of the scrotum or labium majus.
genitofemoral nerve: Arises from L1–L2 and descends on the front of psoas; the efferent limb of the cremasteric reflex.
globus pallidus: Inner part of the lentiform nucleus; the main output station of the basal ganglia.
glossopharyngeal nerve (ix): Carries taste and sensation from the posterior third of the tongue, pharyngeal sensation, the carotid sinus and body, parotid parasympathetic fibres, and supplies stylopharyngeus; the afferent limb of the gag reflex.
gracile fasciculus: Medial dorsal column carrying fine touch, vibration and position sense from the lower trunk and legs.
gracile lobule: Slender lobule of the inferior hemisphere.
Grey matter of the medulla made up of cranial nerve nuclei and relay nuclei.
grey matter of pontine tegmentum: Grey matter in the posterior part of the pons; contains the nuclei of V, VI and VII and the reticular formation.
habenula: Part of the epithalamus; links the limbic system with the brainstem.
hippocampal commissure: Fibres joining the crura of the two fornices.
hippocampus: Fold in the floor of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle; it transfers new information into long-term memory and is among the first regions affected in Alzheimer disease.
hypoglossal nerve (xii): Supplies the tongue muscles; in a peripheral palsy the protruded tongue deviates to the paralysed side.
hypothalamus: Floor and lower walls of the third ventricle; regulates body temperature, hunger and thirst, circadian rhythm and pituitary secretion.
ilio-inguinal nerve: Arises from L1 and passes through the inguinal canal; supplies the skin of the upper inner thigh and external genitalia and can be injured in hernia repair.
iliohypogastric nerve: Arises from L1; gives branches to the abdominal wall muscles and the suprapubic skin.
inferior alveolar nerve: Branch running in the mandibular canal and supplying the lower teeth; blocked in dentistry.
inferior colliculus: Midbrain relay centre of the auditory pathway.
inferior frontal sulcus: Separates the middle and inferior frontal gyri.
inferior lateral brachial cutaneous nerv: Inferior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm
Sensation from the skin of the lower lateral arm.
inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus*: Lower gyrus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe.
inferior salivatory nucleus: Nucleus of the parasympathetic fibres (IX) to the parotid gland.
inferior subscapular nerve: Supplies the lower part of subscapularis and teres major.
inferior temporal gyrus: Gyrus at the lower border of the temporal lobe; takes part in object recognition.
inferior temporal sulcus: Separates the middle and inferior temporal gyri.
inferior trunk of brachial plexus: Formed by the C8–T1 roots; its damage causes Klumpke palsy (claw hand) and it is compressed by a cervical rib or a Pancoast tumour.
infrapatellar branch of saphenous nerve: Sensation from the skin in front of the knee; it can be cut in knee surgery.
insula (subcentral gyrus and ant. and po: Cortex deep in the lateral fissure covered by the opercula; linked to taste, visceral sensation and emotional awareness.
intercostal nerves: Anterior rami of the T1–T11 spinal nerves; they run in the subcostal groove in the order vein–artery–nerve (VAN), so intercostal block is done at the lower border of the rib.
intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of f: Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot
Branch of the superficial fibular nerve to the middle and lateral part of the dorsum of the foot.
intermediolateral nucleus: Sympathetic preganglionic neurons in the lateral horn of T1–L2.
intermediomedial nucleus: Visceral sensory nucleus of the intermediate zone.
interpeduncular fossa: Depression between the two cerebral peduncles; the oculomotor nerve emerges here.
intraparietal sulcus: Separates the superior and inferior parietal lobules.
iris: Muscular diaphragm giving the eye its colour, with the pupil in its centre; it has sphincter (parasympathetic) and dilator (sympathetic) muscles.
lacrimal canaliculus: Thin canal from the punctum on the eyelid margin to the lacrimal sac.
lacrimal gland: Tear-secreting gland in the upper outer corner of the orbit; its parasympathetic fibres come from the facial nerve (pterygopalatine ganglion).
lacrimal sac: Sac in the fossa on the medial wall of the orbit; its inflammation is dacryocystitis.
lat_fis-ant-horizont: Anterior horizontal ramus of lateral sulcus
Horizontal limb of the Sylvian fissure entering the inferior frontal gyrus; it separates the orbital and triangular parts.
lat_fis-ant-vertical: Ascending limb of the Sylvian fissure; it separates the triangular and opercular parts.
lat_fis-post: Long posterior limb of the Sylvian fissure separating the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes.
lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve: Sensory terminal branch of the musculocutaneous nerve; supplies the skin of the lateral forearm.
lateral corticospinal tract: Main pathway of voluntary motor fibres that have crossed in the medulla; damage causes upper motor neuron signs (Babinski) on the same side.
lateral femoral cutaneous nerve: Passes under the inguinal ligament just medial to the ASIS; its compression causes burning on the outer thigh (meralgia paraesthetica).
lateral geniculate body: Thalamic relay nucleus of the visual pathway; the optic radiation goes from here to the occipital cortex.
lateral intermediate substance: Lateral part of the intermediate zone of the spinal cord.
lateral occipital gyrus (middle occipita: Middle gyrus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe.
lateral occipitotemporal gyrus: Gyrus on the inferior surface of the temporal lobe; contains the face recognition area (damage causes prosopagnosia).
lateral pectoral nerve: Arises from the lateral cord and supplies pectoralis major.
lateral plantar nerve: Sensation from the lateral sole and the lateral one and a half toes, and supplies most intrinsic foot muscles (the foot's counterpart of the ulnar nerve).
lateral reticulospinal tract: Pathway from the medullary reticular formation that reduces extensor tone.
lateral spinothalamic tract: Carries pain and temperature from the opposite side; in Brown-Séquard syndrome these are lost on the opposite side.
lateral ventricle: C-shaped cavity in each hemisphere with anterior, posterior and inferior horns and a body; its choroid plexus produces CSF.
lateral vestibulospinal tract: Pathway from the lateral vestibular nucleus stimulating the antigravity extensor muscles.
lens: Transparent lens behind the iris; its shape is changed by the ciliary muscle for accommodation, and its clouding is cataract.
lentiform nucleus: Lens-shaped nucleus formed by the putamen and globus pallidus; lateral to the internal capsule.
lingual gyrus: Gyrus below the calcarine sulcus; it represents the upper visual field.
lingual nerve: Carries general sensation from the anterior two thirds of the tongue and receives taste and parasympathetic fibres from the chorda tympani. It can be injured when extracting lower wisdom teeth.
lingula of cerebellum: Most anterior lobule of the vermis; it lies on the superior medullary velum.
long thoracic nerve: Arises from the C5–C7 roots, runs on the lateral chest wall and supplies serratus anterior; injury during mastectomy causes a winged scapula.
lunate sulcus: Crescent-shaped sulcus sometimes present on the lateral surface of the occipital pole.
mamillary body: Paired swelling on the posterior floor of the hypothalamus; part of the Papez circuit, damaged in Wernicke encephalopathy.
maxillary nerve: Sensory division leaving through the foramen rotundum; supplies the midface, upper teeth, palate and maxillary sinus.
medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve: Carries sensation from the skin of the inner forearm.
medial brachial cutaneous nerve: Nerve from the medial cord carrying sensation from the skin of the inner arm.
medial crural cutaneous branches of saph: Medial crural cutaneous branches of saphenous nerve
Sensation from the inner side of the leg.
